newsitem.title: CHINA: China's first Taiwan-funded bank to open in June.
newsitem.headline: China's first Taiwan-funded bank to open in June.

text.p: First Sino Bank, the first joint venture bank between China and arch rival Taiwan will open for business in Shanghai in mid-June, a bank official said on Friday.
"It is the first bank jointly invested by mainland China and Taiwan," the official told Reuters.
"We plan to start business in mid-June," he said. He declined to give further details.
The bank launched a recruitment drive in Shanghai's official press on Thursday, with an English-language advertisement in the Xinmin Evening News.
The advertisement for managers, dealers and tellers referred to First Sino as "the country's first joint venture bank across the Taiwan Strait".
The two partners in Sino First are Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, with 20 percent, and Lotus Worldwide Ltd with 80 percent, an official of the People's Bank of China has said.
The bank's office will be in Shanghai's premier economic development zone of Pudong, across the Huangpu River from the city centre, the official said.
Beijing has considered Taiwan a renegade province since the communists won the civil war in 1949 and the losing nationalists fled to the island across the Taiwan Strait.
Taiwan has banned direct trade with rival China since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949 although it has allowed commercial ties through other territories, usually Hong Kong.
But it has come under increasing pressure from its own businessmen as well as from Beijing to permit direct shipping and air links.
The two sides have reached agreement on direct crossings between Taiwan's southern port of Kaohsiung and China's port of Xiamen.
